children: J.P. Morgan on Thursday reshuffled its ratings on major equipment-rental companies, upgrading Herc Holdings
while downgrading United Rentals
amid mixed industry conditions and concerns that higher interest rates will delay a recovery in local construction.
Analyst Tami Zakaria raised Herc Holdings
to Overweight from Neutral and established a December 2027 price target of $175. The firm lowered United Rentals
to Neutral from Overweight with a $1,170 target.
J.P. Morgan maintained an Underweight rating on Sunbelt Rentals
, while raising its December 2027 price target to $79 from its previous December 2026 target of $71.
The ratings changes accompanied the introduction of the bank’s 2028 earnings forecasts.
Higher rates lead to mixed picture

J.P. Morgan expects the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates once before the end of 2026. Higher borrowing costs could further postpone a recovery in smaller, locally driven construction markets, which have been sluggish for several years.
At the same time, elevated financing costs may encourage contractors to rent equipment instead of purchasing it. Equipment financing rates already exceed 6%, according to the report.
Demand from mega-projects also remains strong. Rental companies continue to invest in equipment for data centers, energy infrastructure, semiconductor plants and other large developments.
Herc offers integration upside
Herc Holdings

received the most favorable rating in the report. J.P. Morgan believes the company has moved beyond the initial problems associated with its acquisition of H&E Equipment Services and should experience improving fleet utilization.
The bank noted that Herc Holdings’

projected 2026 adjusted EBITDA remains about 10% below the combined companies’ earnings before the transaction. That leaves room for improvement as the integration progresses and the company recovers lost market share.
Herc Holdings
also trades at a wider-than-normal discount to its larger competitors. Its valuation is approximately four EBITDA multiple points below United Rentals
and two points below Sunbelt Rentals
Debt remains the principal concern. Herc Holdings’
leverage exceeds 3.5 times EBITDA, although J.P. Morgan expects that ratio to decline to the low-three-times range by 2027.
The bank forecasts Herc Holdings’

revenue will increase from $5 billion in 2026 to $5.8 billion in 2028. Adjusted EBITDA is projected to rise from $2.1 billion to $2.5 billion, while adjusted earnings are expected to reach $15.11 a share in 2028.
The $175 price target represents about 21% upside from the $144.79 share price cited in the report.
United Rentals’ premium looks full
J.P. Morgan continues to regard United Rentals

as the industry’s best operator, citing its dominant market share, strong margins and financial flexibility. The downgrade reflects valuation and concerns about its future acquisition pipeline rather than a deterioration in the underlying business.
United Rentals

has generated substantial growth through acquisitions during the past decade. However, the shrinking number of large rental companies available for purchase could make it harder to maintain that pace.
The bank said it could become more constructive if United Rentals
resumes sizable acquisitions that supplement organic growth and reduce its exposure to industry cycles.

J.P. Morgan forecasts revenue of $17.8 billion in 2026, $19.4 billion in 2027 and $21.1 billion in 2028. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization is expected to rise from $8.1 billion to $9.7 billion over that period, while earnings are projected to reach $63.35 a share in 2028.
The $1,170 price target offers roughly 13% upside from the report’s reference price of $1,028.77. Even so, the bank believes the shares already reflect United Rentals’
superior business quality.
Sunbelt delivers a strong quarter
Sunbelt Rentals
reported fiscal first-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.18 a share, beating the consensus estimate of $1.04. Revenue rose 11% to $3.12 billion, about 4% above Wall Street expectations.
Adjusted ebitda margin was 42.2%, approximately 60 basis points ahead of consensus. Rental activity associated with the 2026 FIFA World Cup added about 2.5 percentage points to rental revenue growth.
Sunbelt Rentals
raised its adjusted ebitda outlook to between $4.92 billion and $5.12 billion from a previous range of $4.85 billion to $5.05 billion. It also increased its planned investment in rental equipment.

Management described demand as strong across mega-projects, energy, live events and industrial maintenance. Local nonresidential construction remained stable, while rental rates and utilization improved through the quarter.

Still, J.P. Morgan’s longer-term forecasts remain below consensus. The bank believes it is too early to expect a sharp recovery in local construction or rental pricing. It also questioned whether Sunbelt Rentals
can achieve more than 200 basis points of margin expansion by 2029.
The $79 price target implies only about 7% upside from the report’s reference price of $73.42, supporting the Underweight rating.
What it means for investors
J.P. Morgan’s report favors recovery potential over established market leadership. Herc Holdings
carries greater financial and integration risk, but its depressed valuation gives investors more potential upside if execution improves.
United Rentals
remains the highest-quality company in the group, but its premium valuation and a potentially thinner acquisition pipeline limit near-term enthusiasm. Sunbelt Rentals’
strong quarter provides evidence that demand is improving, although J.P. Morgan believes investors are already paying enough for that recovery.

The sector’s outlook ultimately rests on a tug-of-war between interest rates and construction spending. Higher rates may restrain smaller projects, while mega-project investment and the economic appeal of renting instead of buying could keep equipment fleets busy.

title: United Rentals downgraded, Herc upgraded at J.P. Morgan on cloudy outlook
